finding.scope_of_refutation: This attack refutes the CITATION PROVENANCE of the classification thresholds only. It does NOT contest the underlying raw NN-Tanimoto values themselves (0.1579-0.3929 for the 5 candidates), which have been independently re-derived and confirmed correct 6 separate times by prior fires (candidate-structure-identity-audit-v1, R-A07, V-A07, R-A07v2, W-NOV1, V-A07v2) and are not in dispute here. What is refuted is the specific, load-bearing scientific claim that these particular 0.40/0.55/0.75 boundary values are supported by a real published source -- they are not.
finding.statement: The paper actually cited as threshold_source (DOI 10.1186/s13321-015-0069-3, confirmed identity-matched via NCBI's official ID Converter API against the exact DOI) is a comparative study of similarity/distance METRICS (Tanimoto vs Dice vs Cosine vs Soergel vs 4 others), ranked by Sum-of-Ranking-Differences and ANOVA against a composite consensus ranking. Its full text, fetched and verified against real topic-anchor terms ('Sum of ranking differences', 'SRD', 'Dice', 'Cosine coefficient', 'Soergel'), contains ZERO occurrences of 'threshold', 'cutoff', 'weakly similar', 'moderately similar', or the numeric values 0.85, 0.75, 0.55, or 0.40 anywhere in its body. The paper does not propose, discuss, or cite any Tanimoto similarity-value classification scheme for novelty screening. The threshold_source citation attached to every NOVEL/not-NOVEL verdict this module has ever issued is therefore FABRICATED / UNSUPPORTED attribution -- the specific 0.40/0.55/0.75 cutoff values do not trace to the paper named as their source.
